Early, unsigned build of Silly MIDI Tools: a native macOS app that turns audio into MIDI.

## What's new since 0.6.0

This release is about memory and stability. Every model was already loaded for one run and released when it ended; these changes close the gaps around that.

- **Cancel always stops MuScriptor.** Pressing Cancel right after Transcribe, before the engine had started, used to leave it running the whole transcription in the background, holding up to 2.7 GB. Now it never starts.
- **A stuck engine is stopped.** When the MuScriptor engine ignores a stop request, the app still terminates it after 5 seconds, and now kills it 3 seconds later if it is still running. The engine also stops by itself when the app quits or crashes during a run.
- **Less memory during a run.** Piano, the drum models and the drum separator no longer keep every segment's results until the run ends: ten minutes of piano audio held about 240 MB it didn't need. Basic Pitch and Piano prepare one window of audio at a time instead of the whole recording up front. A run's resampled copy of the audio is freed as soon as the run ends.
- **Opening audio uses less memory.** A file is decoded in pieces and mixed to mono as it goes, so a stereo file is no longer held whole first. Opening another file stops a decode that is still going.
- **Audio longer than 1 hour is refused.** The app keeps the whole recording in memory, so a longer file now gets an alert that gives its length and asks you to split it, instead of being opened.
- **Memory warning.** When a model would need more than 40 percent of the Mac's memory while it runs, the inspector says so under the model picker, before anything is downloaded. MuScriptor Large needs about 4.2 GB, so the warning shows on Macs with 8 GB.

## Known limits

- Audio longer than 1 hour can't be opened. Split it into shorter files first.
- Release builds are Apple silicon only, and are not notarized.
- The maintainer's Mac is Intel and cannot run this build, so the arm64 app itself has not been run by hand. The changes were checked in a Debug build on Intel, with and without Address Sanitizer. Please report anything that looks wrong.
